The bug causing `DateUtils.truncate` and `DateUtils.round` to shift dates across Daylight Saving Time (DST) transitions has been resolved.

### Root Cause
During DST transition periods (such as autumn fall-back), invoking `Calendar.set(field, ...)` marks the fields as modified, causing `Calendar` to recalculate its time and resolve ambiguous hours to Standard Time (MST) instead of maintaining Daylight Time (MDT). Additionally:
1. `Calendar.MILLISECOND` was not handled early and went through redundant Calendar operations.
2. Millisecond, second, and minute truncations/roundings were modifying `Calendar` fields directly rather than adjusting epoch milliseconds directly.
3. In the field truncation loop, calling `val.set(field, val.get(field) - offset)` even when `offset == 0` triggered unnecessary recomputation.

### Fix
In [`DateUtils.java`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/lang_65_group_b_fix/src/java/org/apache/commons/lang/time/DateUtils.java#L622-L738):
1. Handled `Calendar.MILLISECOND` directly with an early return.
2. Implemented manual millisecond, second, and minute truncation/rounding by directly modifying the epoch timestamp on `Date`.
3. Guarded `val.set(fields[i][0], val.get(fields[i][0]) - offset)` so that it only executes when `offset != 0`.

- Ran original failing test `org.apache.commons.lang.time.DateUtilsTest::testTruncateLang59`: Passed with 0 failing tests.
